verdict.rationale: Carta publishes its own per-endpoint API reference (cap tables, stakeholders, option grants, convertible notes, FMVs). It also offers a credential-free environment that returns static but valid responses, so examples can be run against something safe. The evidence never shows that the reference pages themselves are interactive (a try-it console or embedded runnable snippets), and the Postman guide relies on an external tool, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: documented in-page interactive try-it console, runnable code examples embedded in the reference, a published OpenAPI spec (probes returned 404), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: Retrieve an issuer's capitalization table by share class.
